The read also yields non-verify.sh run steps: .github/workflows/ci.yml:115 (the `verified` job's ci-verified.py call, a gh/python step with no verify.sh) and the pip install / setup run steps at :226, :246, :271, :293. intent.note: Clause (1): ci.yml:40-43 and CHANGELOG now say a running main run is never cancelled and a queued one is replaced; the return names the option taken (reword). Matches the concurrency block (cancel-in-progress false on main). Clause (2): gate-parity.py _if_tier reduces the `if:` to whole `&&` terms; only !cancelled(), needs.verified.outputs.run=='' and, for release, inputs.tier=='release' are accepted, any other term yields an 'unproved' tier and a problems row naming the job saying its condition cannot be proved to run on every run. A job with no verify.sh call (the push-only `verified` guard) hits `continue` before the check and stays outside. All real ci.yml conditions (lines 101, 145-306) are of these shapes. Clause (3): ci-verified.py VOUCHING_EVENTS/_can_vouch accepts only workflow_dispatch and push; decide() appends a why naming the event; ask_github skips the jobs fetch for a non-vouching run (cv18 asserts the jobs path of the pull_request run is not asked and the push run's is). Clause (4): grep -n 'ci.yml' on both files returns nothing; the slices named, `e2e` (verify.sh:418, its 'the TDD nudge, through the launcher' step at :534) and `manifests` (:591, scale_demo_valid at :726), exist in verify.sh. Clause (5): SKILL.md names `sh tools/verify.sh --list`. The executor's claim (7 files, option reword, cv18/sv12) describes the diff; only the SKILL.md sentence overstates the workflow slightly (finding 1).
